chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked:
about the killing of the stone and the almond (or the fruit thereof), whether it is permissible to eat from it? He said, 'No.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the stone or fruit of al-bundugh according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on consuming the 'al-bundugh' (often identified as the pomegranate stone or a specific fruit/nut) after its separation or 'killing' (harvesting). The Imam’s negative response ('La') establishes a specific prohibition, distinguishing this item from general permissible foods and highlighting the precision of Shia fiqh in dietary laws. This ruling underscores the importance of distinguishing between the edible parts of produce and those deemed impure or prohibited by the Imams.
